problem: The first full run was interrupted by a network outage while the machine slept.
fix: Added --resume to rerun only failed or missing runs.

problem: Phoenix named every code evaluator "evaluator", collapsing them into one column.
Resumed runs kept the failed attempt's grade.
fix: backfill_evals.py redoes any evaluation older than its run.

problem: Concurrent agents exceeded OpenRouter's 20 requests per minute per model.
fix: Per-model rate limiter; latency metrics exclude queue time.

problem: Phoenix cost columns showed $0 for OpenRouter model ids.
fix: register_pricing.py adds OpenRouter prices to Phoenix's model table.

problem: Phoenix doesn't price decision-model spans; they report decision.* token counts, not llm.*.
fix: The agent computes each decision's cost itself and records it as decision.cost_usd.

problem: When a Claude model both decided and wrote text, routing and writing costs blended together.
fix: Each decider LLM gets its own usage accounting, separate from the generator.

problem: Running the full suite would have rerun, and paid again for, the seven pilot questions.
fix: Split the Phoenix dataset into pilot and main, then copied the pilot runs into the full experiments with merge_pilot.py.

problem: Microsoft and OpenAI decision models reject choice questions with fewer than two options.
fix: Ask which result to read only when two or more are unread.

problem: Phoenix returned uploaded metadata as strings, so "False" read as true.
fix: Restore real types before the evaluators read them.

problem: One Haiku routing call stalled for 2.2 hours, skewing its latency.
fix: Excluded Haiku from the latency charts.
